{{nihongo|'''Suearata Shrine'''|陶荒田神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izumi Province]].

'''Suearata Shrine''' (すえあらたじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in Ueno, {{ill|Naka-ku, Sakai|ca|Naka (Sakai)|es|Naka-ku (Sakai)|fa|ناکا-کو، ساکای|fr|Naka-ku (Sakai)|it|Naka-ku (Sakai)|ja|中区 (堺市)|ko|나카구 (사카이시)|th|เขตนากะ (ซาไก)|tr|Naka, Sakai|zh|中區 (堺市)|zh_yue|中區 (堺市)|qid=Q1042487|lt=Naka-ku}}, {{ill|Sakai|ar|ساكاي|arz|ساكاى (تجمع سكان فى محافظه اوساكا)|ban|Sakai, Osaka|be|Сакаі (Осака)|bg|Сакаи|br|Sakai|ca|Sakai (Osaka)|ce|Сакаи (Осака)|ceb|Sakai Shi|cs|Sakai (Ósaka)|cy|Sakai|da|Sakai|de|Sakai|eo|Sakaj|es|Sakai (Osaka)|et|Sakai|eu|Sakai (Osaka)|fa|ساکای، اوساکا|fi|Sakai|fr|Sakai|ga|Sakai|gl|Sakai, Osaka|he|סאקאי|hu|Szakai (Oszaka)|hy|Սակաի|id|Sakai, Osaka|it|Sakai (Osaka)|ja|堺市|ki|Sakai|ko|사카이시 (오사카부)|la|Sacaium|lt|Sakajus|mg|Sakai|mn|Сакай|ms|Sakai|nl|Sakai (Osaka)|no|Sakai|os|Сакаи (Осакæ)|pl|Sakai (Osaka)|pt|Sakai (Osaka)|ro|Sakai, Osaka|ru|Сакаи (Осака)|sah|Сакаи|sco|Sakai|sh|Sakai, Osaka|simple|Sakai, Osaka|sk|Sakai (Osaka)|sr|Сакај|su|Sakai, Osaka|sv|Sakai|tg|Сакаи|th|ซาไก (เมือง)|tl|Sakai, Osaka|tr|Sakai|tt|Сакаи (Осака)|tum|Sakai|uk|Сакай (Осака)|ur|ساکائی، اوساکا|uz|Sakai|vi|Sakai|war|Sakai|wuu|堺市|zh|堺市|zh_classical|堺市|zh_min_nan|Sakai-chhī (Tāi-pán)|zh_yue|堺市|qid=Q193428}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}, and a Shikinaisha of {{ill|Ōtori district|ja|大鳥郡|zh|大鳥郡|qid=Q3270651}}, {{ill|Izumi Province|ca|Província d'Izumi|ckb|پارێزگای ئیزومی|cs|Provincie Izumi|de|Provinz Izumi|es|Provincia de Izumi|fa|ولایت ایزومی|fr|Province d'Izumi|gl|Provincia de Izumi|hak|Izumi-koet|id|Provinsi Izumi|it|Izumi (provincia)|ja|和泉国|ko|이즈미국|lt|Idzumio žemė|nl|Izumi (provincie)|pt|Província de Izumi|ru|Идзуми (провинция)|simple|Izumi Province|sk|Izumi (provincia)|sr|Провинција Изуми|tr|Izumi (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ідзумі|zh|和泉國|zh_min_nan|Izumi-kok|zh_yue|和泉國|qid=Q1047117}}.

It stands in the birthplace area of {{ill|Sue pottery|Q7634351|qid=Q7634351}} (the ancestor of Japanese pottery), and is also called '''Tōki Ōmiya'''. It is famous as the Ebisu of pottery, and the January Hatsu-Ebisu festival draws many people from technical, manufacturing, and commercial fields.

=== Origin ===
In Sujin 8 (90 BCE), {{ill|Emperor Sujin|Q333530|qid=Q333530}} chose {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōtataneko}} living in the Ōta forest of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sue Village}} as chief priest. This shrine was founded to enshrine his ancestral spirits, and is considered to have been founded around Sujin 8.

At that time, a major epidemic spread and the land was devastated. One night, deity {{ill|Ōmononushi|lt=Ōmononushi|Q10936701|qid=Q10936701}} appeared in Emperor Sujin’s dream and said that if Ōtataneko were appointed priest and worship offered, the disease would be calmed. The emperor found Ōtataneko in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Chinu Agata}}{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sue Village}} and appointed him priest of {{ill|Mount Miwa|Q860627|qid=Q860627}} in Nara to worship Ōmononushi.

The shrine name is said to derive from “{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Areta no Atai}},” who lived in the Ōta forest of the same Sue Village. Areta no Atai is said to have been a direct descendant of Takamimusubi-no-Mikoto, one of the enshrined deities.
